title: Finite locally free surjections reflect ampleness of the supplied line
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a surjective finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Thus $f$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, and is surjective on underlying points. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If its tensor pullback $f^*L$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample, then $L$ is ample, both in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No properness, normality, Noetherianity or constant-degree hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), and 0BD0 (lemma-norm-ample, its proof for the specified norm line); Norm_f(f^*L)=L^{\otimes d}, applied on the open-and-closed constant-rank pieces.

proof.text: Put $M=f^*L$. By the definition of ampleness, $Y$ is quasi-compact. For an open cover of $X$, its inverse images cover $Y$; a finite subcover of $Y$ covers $X$ because $f$ is surjective. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact. If $X$ is empty the affine-section condition is vacuous, so $L$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 0BD0 (divisors-lemma-norm-ample), quasi-compactness paragraph; empty case from the definition.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. Apply the locally constant rank assertion to $f$, and put $d=r_f(x)$ and $U=r_f^{-1}(d)$. Then $U$ is open and closed and contains $x$. Moreover $d>0$: a point of $Y$ over $x$ exists by surjectivity, so the fibre algebra admits a unital map to the nonzero residue field of that point, which therefore cannot have dimension zero. Write $Y_U=f^{-1}U$ and $f_U:Y_U\to U$. Restriction to an open of the target keeps the same finite, flat, finitely presented affine algebra charts, so $f_U$ is finite locally free of degree $d$; the fibre dimensions are unchanged. Choose an affine open $V$ of $X$ containing $x$ and contained in $U$, using the affine-open basis of a scheme.

source.place: Tag 04MH (morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free), degree strata; Tag 0BD2 applied on a positive-degree stratum.

proof.text: The fibre $E=f^{-1}(\{x\})$ is finite. Apply the finite-set ample-section lemma to the ample line $M$ on the whole scheme $Y$ and the open $W=f^{-1}V$. It gives $n>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ with $E\subseteq Y_s\subseteq f^{-1}V$. Restrict $s$ to $Y_U$. Pullback composition identifies $M|_{Y_U}$ with $f_U^*(L|_U)$, and its tensor powers restrict by the tensor section formula. Apply the norm-section lemma to $f_U,L|_U,n,s|_{Y_U}$. Obtain $t_U\in\Gamma(U,(L|_U)^{\otimes(dn)})$ with $U_{t_U}=\{z\in U:f^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq Y_s\}$. Hence $x\in U_{t_U}\subseteq V$: the first inclusion uses $E\subseteq Y_s$; for the second, lift $z$ to a point $y$ using surjectivity, so $y\in Y_s\subseteq f^{-1}V$ implies $z\in V$.

source.place: Tag 0BD0 (divisors-lemma-norm-ample), finite-fibre section and its norm; Tags 0BD2, 0BCY, 0BCZ for the specified line.

proof.text: On the disjoint open cover $X=U\cup(X\setminus U)$, glue $t_U$ and the zero section of $L^{\otimes(dn)}|_{X\setminus U}$. The sheaf axiom applies because their overlap is empty. This gives a global $t\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes(dn)})$ with $X_t=U_{t_U}\subseteq V$ and $x\in X_t$. The affine-cap-section lemma gives $V\cap X_t=X_t$ affine. Since $dn>0$, this is a global positive-power affine-section witness for $L$ at $x$. Together with step 1 and the definition of ampleness, the witnesses for all $x$ prove $L$ ample.
